Girl, 2, falls to death from 5th floor  NYC apartment window in tragic accident

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A 2-year-old Bronx girl fell to her death from a fifth-floor apartment window in what appears to be a tragic accident late Tuesday, cops and sources said.

The toddler plunged from the window on the top floor of the building on East 138th Street near St. Ann’s Avenue in Mott Haven around 10:45 p.m., police said.

She landed in an alleyway and was rushed unconscious to Harlem Hospital, where she succumbed to her injuries.

The tot apparently took the fall after pushing aside the divider between the window and the air conditioner, the sources said.

Her mother was in another room when her young daughter fell, and ultimately called 911.

No criminality is suspected in the deadly fall, cops said.

[Source 2 — www.abc.net.au (Bias: Center / Public Broadcaster)] (URL: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-11-05/federal-court-challenge-to-adelaide-motogp-circuit-falls-over/107349314):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Federal Court challenge to Adelaide MotoGP circuit falls over

A case brought by a Queensland man against the SA government's plans for a MotoGP circuit in Adelaide has been discontinued.

Actual Article Body:
Emergency

Backstory

Newsletters

中文新闻

BERITA BAHASA INDONESIA

TOK PISIN

Topic:Courts

Construction is due to begin on the Adelaide MotoGP circuit in December. (Supplied: SA Government)

An interstate challenge to South Australia's Adelaide Circuit project has been withdrawn, following a brief hearing in Brisbane.

Neither the federal or South Australian governments will pursue costs.

The SA government faces another challenge to the project, to be heard in the state's Supreme Court later this month.

A Queensland man's Federal Court challenge against the South Australian government's MotoGP circuit has been discontinued.

Joshua Hogan lodged action in the Federal Court in September seeking a permanent injunction against the proposed $96 million Adelaide circuit, which will require the removal of nearly 400 trees and is due to begin construction in December.

But at a brief hearing on Thursday morning, Judicial Registrar Michael Buckingham said the proceedings "were going to be discontinued".

Asked if any of the parties had anything to add, Mr Hogan said: "I'm fine, I just want to get this over my depression's pretty bad."

Judicial Registrar Buckingham replied that he understood and he "hoped this proceeding would come to an end for everyone's sake very quickly".

The state and federal governments are not seeking costs from Mr Hogan.

Premier Peter Malinauskas said the SA government was "very grateful" Mr Hogan's case had been discontinued.

"[This is] another legal hurdle that we've now overcome when it comes to the MotoGP circuit development," he said.

Mr Hogan had lodged his application against the development of the Adelaide Circuit in the federal court in Brisbane. (ABC News: Rachel Riga)

A separate legal challenge to the circuit by the South East City Residents Association (SECRA) remains ongoing.

The SA Supreme Court today set down a hearing for the matter on November 17, according to SECRA president David Klingberg.

Mr Klingberg said the discontinuation of the Queensland Federal Court challenge "doesn't affect" SECRA's case, which is based on the state government's powers under the Motorsport Act.

"Clearly … the government doesn't have the power to cut down trees," Mr Klingberg said.

"The Act is all about promoting motorsports and our view is they can do that to their heart's content on existing infrastructure."

Mr Malinauskas, asked if he was confident that state government could overcome the SECRA legal challenge, said: "I hope so, but I never pre-empt the outcomes of courts."

"We've done all the work, we've done it as thoroughly as possible, we've worked really hard to engage with local communities, the … Conservation Council to get a good outcome here," he said.

"People are entitled to take up whatever action they so choose, it's part of a healthy liberal democracy and a functioning judicial system.

"That's oversight that we're not against, we welcome it."

MotoGP is due to be hosted in Adelaide in November 2027.
